## 1. ATL-GEM-01 · Atlas: the Federal Reserve bank holidays 2026 to 2030, as observed (55 rows) to check the payday arithmetic

**Due:** 2026-12-05 · **State:** now

**Why:** Atlas moves a payday that falls on a bank holiday to the business day before (pillars/atlas/pay.js). Its holiday list is computed; it needs an outside list to be checked against.

**What it unlocks:** A unit test that compares Atlas's holidays with the Federal Reserve's own list for five years.

**Read first:**
- https://www.frbservices.org/about/holiday-schedules
- pillars/atlas/pay.js in jpavia10/prometheus-hub (the rules it uses, top of the file)

**Do this:**
1. For each year 2026, 2027, 2028, 2029 and 2030, list the 11 holidays on the Federal Reserve's schedule.
2. Give the calendar date and the date the Federal Reserve is closed (a Sunday holiday is observed on the Monday; a Saturday one is not moved).
3. Where the schedule for a year is not published yet, take the rule from the page that states it and say so in the note.

**Make:** `atlas_gemini_bank-holidays_{YYYYMMDD-HHMM}.json`

**Save in:** Prometheus Hub/Pillars/Prometheus Hub/incoming (AI drop files)/

**Shape:** `JSON array, one object per row, exactly the fields below`

**Every field, exactly:**
- `n` (number): 1, 2, 3 ...
- `year` (number): 2026 to 2030
- `holiday` (text): its name on the schedule
- `date` (date): the calendar date, YYYY-MM-DD
- `closed` (date or none): the day the Federal Reserve is closed for it, or none for a Saturday
- `note` (text): empty, or why
- `source_url` (url): the official page that shows the value (a .gov, the statute, or the agency's own page)
- `checked` (date): the day you read it, YYYY-MM-DD

**How many:** 55

**Done when:** 55 rows, 11 a year for five years.

**How Claude checks it:**
- Claude runs every row through ATLAS_PAY.holidays() and every difference is either a fix to pay.js or a rejected row.

**Not done (sent back) if:**
- a value without a source URL that shows it
- rows missing to reach the count
- a source that is a blog, forum, law-firm marketing page or AI summary where an official page exists
- a value for a year that has not been published yet presented as if it had (write "not published as of {date}" instead)

## 2. ATL-GEM-02 · Atlas: the 2026 and 2027 payroll numbers for a California employee (wage bases, rates, plan limits) with their official pages

**Due:** 2026-12-07 · **State:** now

**Why:** Atlas checks each pay stub's withholding. The rates and caps change every year: Social Security's wage base, Medicare's extra 0.9 % threshold, California SDI's rate and wage base, the 401(k), HSA and FSA limits.

**What it unlocks:** Atlas can say when a stub's Social Security stops (the wage base is reached) and what the year's plan limits are.

**Read first:**
- https://www.ssa.gov/oact/cola/cbb.html
- https://www.irs.gov (the 401(k), HSA, FSA and Medicare pages)
- https://edd.ca.gov (the SDI rate and taxable wage limit page)

**Do this:**
1. For each year 2026 and 2027 give: Social Security tax rate and wage base; Medicare rate; Additional Medicare tax rate and its thresholds (single, joint); California SDI rate and taxable wage limit; 401(k) elective deferral limit and the age-50 catch-up; the age 60 to 63 catch-up; HSA self-only and family limits; health FSA limit.
2. One row per number. A 2027 number not yet published: say so in the note, value empty.

**Make:** `atlas_gemini_payroll-numbers_{YYYYMMDD-HHMM}.json`

**Save in:** Prometheus Hub/Pillars/Prometheus Hub/incoming (AI drop files)/

**Shape:** `JSON array, one object per row, exactly the fields below`

**Every field, exactly:**
- `n` (number): 1, 2, 3 ...
- `year` (number): 2026 or 2027
- `item` (text): what it is, as named above
- `value` (number or empty): a rate as a decimal (0.062), dollars as a number
- `note` (text): empty, or not published / the condition
- `source_url` (url): the official page that shows the value (a .gov, the statute, or the agency's own page)
- `checked` (date): the day you read it, YYYY-MM-DD

**How many:** 24

**Done when:** Both years, every item above.

**How Claude checks it:**
- Claude opens every source URL and checks the value.

**Not done (sent back) if:**
- a value without a source URL that shows it
- rows missing to reach the count
- a source that is a blog, forum, law-firm marketing page or AI summary where an official page exists
- a value for a year that has not been published yet presented as if it had (write "not published as of {date}" instead)

## 3. ATL-GEM-03 · Atlas: California pay rules that touch a paycheck and time off (Labor Code), with the statute for each

**Due:** 2026-12-09 · **State:** now

**Why:** Atlas tells Joseph when a stub or a time-off balance looks wrong. In California a vacation cap is allowed but forfeiting earned vacation is not, a stub must show set items, and paydays have legal deadlines.

**What it unlocks:** Atlas's stub check can list what a California stub must show, and its time-off panel can say what happens to vacation at a cap and when leaving a job.

**Read first:**
- https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov (Labor Code sections 201, 202, 203, 204, 226, 227.3, 246)
- https://www.dir.ca.gov/dlse/ (the DLSE's own FAQ pages on vacation, paydays and pay stubs)

**Do this:**
1. One row per rule: the paydays a month and how soon after the pay period wages are due (204); final pay when fired and when quitting (201, 202) and the waiting-time penalty (203); each item a pay stub must show (226), one row per item; vacation: no forfeiture, caps allowed, paid out at the end (227.3 and the DLSE vacation FAQ); paid sick leave: how much and how it accrues (246, as amended).

**Make:** `atlas_gemini_ca-pay-rules_{YYYYMMDD-HHMM}.json`

**Save in:** Prometheus Hub/Pillars/Prometheus Hub/incoming (AI drop files)/

**Shape:** `JSON array, one object per row, exactly the fields below`

**Every field, exactly:**
- `n` (number): 1, 2, 3 ...
- `topic` (text): paydays, final pay, pay stub, vacation or sick leave
- `rule` (text): the rule in one plain sentence
- `section` (text): Labor Code section
- `quote` (text): the words of the statute or the DLSE page that say it, copied exactly
- `source_url` (url): the official page that shows the value (a .gov, the statute, or the agency's own page)
- `checked` (date): the day you read it, YYYY-MM-DD

**How many:** 20

**Done when:** At least 20 rows covering all five topics, every pay-stub item one row.

**How Claude checks it:**
- Claude opens ten source URLs at random and finds each quote on the page.

**Not done (sent back) if:**
- a value without a source URL that shows it
- rows missing to reach the count
- a source that is a blog, forum, law-firm marketing page or AI summary where an official page exists
- a value for a year that has not been published yet presented as if it had (write "not published as of {date}" instead)
- a quote that is not on the page word for word
